questions.stem: Which combination best explains why Metacom's War began in 1675?

choices.text: Metacom commanded every Native community to follow one unified plan, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Metacom was important, but leaders and communities retained distinct authority and made changing choices.

choices.text: The war began only because colonists wanted captives to sell, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: The captive market shaped the war's consequences, but the evidence does not support it as the single cause.

choices.text: One unexplained attack created a conflict in an otherwise stable region, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: The region was already destabilized by land, jurisdiction, religion, and mistrust.

choices.text: Land loss, colonial jurisdiction, religious pressure, mistrust, and local escalation narrowed peaceful choices.
choices.feedback: This multi-cause explanation distinguishes underlying pressures from the Sassamon case and Swansea violence that helped ignite war.

questions.conciseCorrectFeedback: Exactly. This is the strongest cause answer.
questions.conciseIncorrectFeedback: Not quite. Focus on the cause relationship the question is testing.

This multi-cause explanation distinguishes underlying pressures from the Sassamon case and Swansea violence that helped ignite war.

questions.stem: Why is 'Metacom's War' still an imperfect name for the conflict?

choices.text: English colonists never used the name King Philip, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Colonists commonly called him Philip and remembered the conflict as King Philip's War.

choices.text: The conflict involved only Plymouth and one Wampanoag village, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: It became a many-sided regional war involving numerous Native and colonial communities.

choices.text: It restores a Native name but can still imply that one sachem commanded many independent leaders and communities.
choices.feedback: The name is useful only when paired with the conflict's political plurality.

choices.text: Metacom was not involved in the war, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Metacom was an important leader, though not an absolute commander.

questions.stem: Why was the Great Swamp Fight a major turning point?

choices.text: It separated civilians completely from the fighting, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Many women and children were killed, and the attack blurred combatant distinctions.

choices.text: A colonial attack on a Narragansett winter stronghold killed many people and helped push survivors into the widening war.
choices.feedback: The attack shows how preventive destruction could create the larger enemy colonists feared.

choices.text: It ended the war immediately with no further attacks, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: The war continued and expanded after the attack.

choices.text: It proved the Narragansett had commanded the conflict from the start, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Narragansett leaders had attempted an unstable neutrality before the assault.

choices.text: English firearms made local knowledge irrelevant, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern, across the political and social setting examined here.

questions.stem: Which factor best explains the Pueblo Revolt's broad appeal in 1680?

choices.text: One Pueblo community obeyed a single inherited monarchy, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Pueblo peoples had distinct communities and political traditions; coordination had to be built.

choices.text: Spanish officials had ended missionary punishment and tribute, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Coercion and demands were central grievances rather than resolved problems.

choices.text: The revolt depended entirely on horses first acquired in 1680, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Horses circulated before the revolt, though the upheaval accelerated wider dispersal.

choices.text: Religious coercion, punishment, drought, raids, and colonial demands produced a crisis in Spanish authority across Pueblo communities.
choices.feedback: This explains why coordinated resistance could draw strength from several linked pressures.

questions.stem: How should historians use testimony taken by Spanish officials after the Pueblo Revolt?

choices.text: Reject it completely because Spaniards recorded it, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: A compromised source can still preserve evidence when read critically.

choices.text: Use only details that confirm Spanish claims about sorcery, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Spanish categories must be analyzed rather than accepted as neutral descriptions.

choices.text: Read it as valuable but coerced and layered evidence shaped by translation, interrogation, and Spanish categories.
choices.feedback: This approach neither discards the testimony nor mistakes it for an unfiltered Native voice.

choices.text: Treat every recorded sentence as a verbatim transcript, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Interrogation, translation, and colonial recording shaped the surviving words.

questions.stem: What was the most important short-term consequence of the Pueblo Revolt?

choices.text: Catholicism disappeared completely from every Pueblo community, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Religious change was complex; revolt did not erase all earlier influence or later adaptation.

choices.text: Pueblo forces expelled Spanish rule from New Mexico for about twelve years and restored room for Native political and religious action.
choices.feedback: The revolt demonstrated that colonial rule could be removed, even though unity and independence faced limits.

choices.text: Spain permanently abandoned all claims west of the Mississippi, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Spain reconquered New Mexico beginning in the 1690s.

choices.text: Every Pueblo community remained united under one government, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Communities had distinct interests, and post-revolt unity was difficult to sustain.

choices.text: Native exchange and political networks moved horses widely, and the revolt accelerated processes already underway.
choices.feedback: This centers Native agency instead of treating animals as gifts that spread only through imperial control.

choices.text: Horses had no presence north of Mexico before 1680, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.

choices.text: Spanish officials directed every stage of horse movement, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Native exchange, raiding, breeding, and diplomacy helped drive dispersal.

choices.text: The revolt stopped horses from moving beyond New Mexico, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: The upheaval helped widen access and circulation.

choices.text: Metacom's War mechanically caused every accusation sixteen years later, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.

choices.text: Frontier violence had no connection to accusers or accused people, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: The experiences of Mercy Lewis and George Burroughs make the connection historically significant.

choices.text: Frontier-war trauma and fear mattered strongly, but they interacted with local conflict, religion, gender, politics, and legal choices.
choices.feedback: This treats the war interpretation as powerful without turning it into a single-cause verdict.

choices.text: Every accused person confessed at once, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Confession did not produce a universal or immediate end.

choices.text: Frontier warfare ended permanently in 1692, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: War and fear continued beyond Salem.

choices.text: The same evidentiary rules remained in place and produced the opposite result.
choices.feedback: Changing acceptance of evidence and authority helped stop prosecutions.

questions.stem: Why did some English captives choose not to return permanently?

choices.text: Captives were biologically unable to remember English society, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: The issue was social belonging and life experience, not biology.

choices.text: Every captive was held under continuous physical force for life, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Some captives were adopted and later chose their communities even when return was possible.

choices.text: New England offered no attempts at redemption or return, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Families and governments repeatedly sought to recover captives.

choices.text: Adoption, kinship, language, religion, marriage, and daily life could create durable belonging in Native or French communities.
choices.feedback: This explains refusal as a meaningful social choice rather than simple confusion.
